{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Identity" },
  "read": "This student put in real effort and still came up short, which is the most demoralizing kind of failure. They are not being lazy — they are protecting themselves from trying again and getting hurt again. The 'I'm just bad at this' story is a shield: if the problem is fixed ability, they never have to risk effort and failure again. Status is threatened too, because they may feel foolish for studying hard and having nothing to show for it.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Lower the bar or over-reassure them with 'you'll get it next time' — which sounds kind but signals you don't actually believe the standard is within their reach, and they will sense that." },
  "mentorMove": "Hold the standard exactly where it is, but shift the story from fixed ability to fixable strategy — the brain grew during that study session even if the score didn't show it yet, and the job now is to find the gap in approach, not confirm a verdict on talent.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "The standard for what counts as mastering this material stays the same — you are not adjusting it down.",
    "You are not accepting 'I'm just bad at this' as a final answer; that framing goes unchallenged only when you stay quiet."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "How they study next time is completely open — different resources, study partners, practice formats, coming to you with specific questions.",
    "When and where the follow-up conversation happens can flex around what works for them."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 1, "label": "Empathy" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I saw your score and I could tell it didn't match the work you put in. That is genuinely frustrating, and I want you to know I noticed you prepared." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Can I ask — when you were studying, what did that actually look like? Walk me through it for a second." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Okay, so here is what I'm seeing: the effort was real, but I think we can find the gap in the method, not in you. That's actually a solvable problem. Let's figure out one thing to change before the next one." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I'm not letting you off the hook on this material, and I'm not doing that because I think you can't get there — I'm doing it because I'm pretty sure you can. I have high standards for you specifically, and I'd rather work with you on the how than watch you decide the story is already over." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Every time this student tries again after a setback, point out that the trying itself is the skill that compounds — not the score on any single attempt. Over time, catching them applying a new strategy and naming it out loud will do more for their belief in their own competence than any single good grade."
}
situation: A student who clearly studied did poorly and is convinced they are just bad at this subject.
